questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go far away and explore a place I had never really been before. I wanted to go to a place where you were able to speak English as I thought it would be easier to make local friends when they spoke English. And I didn't want to go to the US.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been amazing! One of the biggest expierences in my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I think Deakin was quite good at providing information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Intro events for foreign exchange students and when if I had any issues I could alwaus sent an email to the exchange coordinator e.g. when I wnated to change units. That was very helpfull.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not that easy but you have to remain calm. We were lucky to find a place via Facebook. My friend is another Danish guy whom I had worked with a little bit in Denmark in our gap-year and he made a facebook post and we were lucky that our landlord had good expeirences with Danish students renting her house so she contacted my friend and we ended up renting her house in Fitzroy together with 3 other Danes. So definetly check the facebook groups for housing in Melbourne e.g. Fairy Floss.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was very happy with living in Fitzroy which is a very nice area like Nørrebro. It is a bit far commute to Deakin University but you really only have to be on campus 2-3 days a week so I would rather stay in a nice area in the city in stead of staying in Burwood/on campus which is quite expensive and far away from the city. Both has pros and cons but whenever you want to do something or go out you really want to do it in the city or the inner Nothern suburbs - so I would rather stay in those areas and have a longer commute to Uni rather than the other way around.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is hard to find, and it can be expensive but it is possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: that was fine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a unit-catalouge and you should choose which you wanted but you can also change in the first weeks of the semester which was nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Quite easy to sent an email to the exhange-student-coordinator and she was very hepfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: pick units that you think would interest you and that is not offered back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good. you have to get used to doing a lot more assignments than back home, but the exam periods are easier on the other hand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt like the academic level was lower than in Copenhagen but you end up spending as much or even more time on Uni-stuff because there are so many assignments that requires time and energy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: So it is a quite different way of learning beacuse it requires more of you in a sense beacuse you have to do more assignments compared to back home. Furthermore it is much more practical/business focues compared to the more teoretical aproach in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AIR350 - Australia And The Indo-Pacific Identity Interests And Order

MMM132 - Management

ALR214 - Lobbying And Advocacy

SLE308 Policy Instruments for Sustainability

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
SLE308 Policy Instruments for Sustainability was very nice. It consited of two was of looking at sustainbility and envoirment policies both from a government and a business point of view. Government aspect was essentially policy analysis aplied on climate and envoirmental issues. And the businesses aspect was around building an envoirmental management system and how to consult companies and businesses and transitioning to more green solutions. I Found that quite fun. 

The Australia And The Indo-Pacific Identity Interests And Order was also fun because you get to see Australian foreign policy and IR through a different perspective than the European/Danish.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to travel around Australia but totally worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee is very good and very cheap compared to Denmark. 

Beer and alcohol in general is quite expensive but wine is relatively cheap. 

Otherwise it is quite similar to Danish prices, some. groceries beeing a little cheaper while others are a little more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good, but I lived so far from the campus that I didn't really use it that much. I played football on the team for a while and it was nice but I in  the end the commute was too far for me so I stopped .

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Several Clubs and associations e.g. football, Footie, cycling etc. 

There is an introduction party in the O week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Good idea to join some of the clubs e.g. football club or mountenering club or surfing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore all of Melbourne, there is so many lovely suburbs and areas! And then travel a lot around Australia! east coast is brillant and Tasmania was extraordinary, probably some of the most unique places I have ever been. Big recomendation. 

Buy/rent outdoor/camping gear and go camping and hiking in Victoria e.g. in the Grampain Mountains, Great ocean road or the Dandenong ranges.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is very western but with their own unique Aussie elements.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend to the seminars and engage in the group work. It is not so easy but it can be done and I think evryone is very friendly and openmindied - more so than in Denmark. I met a lot of lovely local students in some of my units. But in some of the units there is quite an age gap between the students which can have an effect on how much you want to socialize with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are generally a bit younger at Uni and the age gap can sometimes be a bit big. But they are sweet nonetheless.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are so open and welcoming and very nice. Very helpfull and a "no worries mate" kind of culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be open and willing to try new things and meet new people.
2) Enjoy and go travel and explore Australia!
3) Highly consider living in the city/inner northern suburbs in stead of staying out on campus. It can be stressfull not to have a place before leaving Denmark but you will find one and I recon it is much nicer to live in the city rather than out in Burwood.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you are spending a lot more time on assignments compared to UCPH and that often you dont really have exams but rather 3-4 assignments during the semester in stead.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting so many new and wonderfull people and getting to know a different kind of culture and country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There is so much to see and do in this wonderfull country. And you want to see as much of it as you can. But there is also a lot of assignments that requires time and energy - and that can be hard to balance at times and you can get tired of writing assignemnts.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO GO GO - it is amazing in Melbourne!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
